claim: For every fixed q>=2, the exact projected uniform q-state row-urn code likelihood on an explicit full-span binary block with each positive gap value occurring at most twice has a polynomial-bit FPRAS in N, epsilon^-1 and log(delta^-1).
inputs_and_proof: One explicit N-bit binary block with events at 1, 1+g_1, ..., N; q is fixed and known as part of the theorem family. The generic code chooses a uniform anchor in {1,...,N-S}; full span forces anchor 1. The separate allzero mode outputs 0^N. At N=1, K_{1,q}=2 and the one-event probability is 1/2. No hidden states, pool, source parameter, code oracle or succinct horizon is supplied. Proof in RESULT.txt and independent reconstruction in AUDIT.txt.
cost: Correction mean is at least (3/4)128^(-2(q-1))(m+1)^(-5(q-1)); fixed-q correction DP is O_q(m^q) integer operations per sample. A deliberately coarse JS-derived arithmetic bound for the correction phase is O_q(m^(15(q-1)+16) epsilon^-4 log(delta^-1) polylog(m/epsilon,delta^-1)); finite-bit rational simulation is internally reconstructed, not executable/benchmarked.
baseline_and_failure: Exact hidden-path summation is the direct exponential baseline. No result for growing q, multiplicity >=3, censored prefixes, suffix prediction, generic hidden-renewal reconstruction, AP-hardness, or approximation hardness. The theorem is a likelihood computation, not a teacher-free learner.
novelty: UNKNOWN; no firstness, priority, or external proof validation claim.
